subproblem.title: Blow-up domains η_{x,λ_i}(U) eventually contain every bounded set
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P, every x ∈ U, every sequence (λ_i)_{i∈ℕ} of reals with λ_i > 0 for all i and λ_i → 0, and every bounded set K ⊆ ℝ^P (Bornology.IsBounded K): for all sufficiently large i, K ⊆ η_{x,λ_i}(U), where η_{x,λ}(y) = λ^{−1}(y − x) is Simon's dilation (Lean dilation x λ y = −(λ⁻¹ • x) + λ⁻¹ • y), i.e. ∀ᶠ i in atTop, K ⊆ dilation x (λ_i) '' U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ), IsOpen U → x ∈ U → (∀ i, 0 < lams i) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), Bornology.IsBounded K → ∀ᶠ i in atTop, K ⊆ dilation x (lams i) '' U
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the domain claims in steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof ('tsupport dω lies in the domain η_{x,σ_i}(U) of blowUp T x σ_i for all large i (x ∈ U, U open, σ_i → 0)' and 'B_{δ'}(v) lies in the domain of blowUp T x σ_i for large i'). Notation: η_{x,λ}(y) = λ^{−1}(y − x); in Lean dilation x λ y = −(λ⁻¹ • x) + dilationCLM P λ y with dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹ • id.
1. Since U is open and x ∈ U, there is δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). Since K is bounded, there is r ∈ ℝ with K ⊆ closedBall(0, r) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall), i.e. |w| ≤ r for every w ∈ K.
2. As λ_i → 0, also λ_i·(|r| + 1) → 0·(|r| + 1) = 0; since δ > 0, λ_i·(|r| + 1) < δ for all sufficiently large i.
3. Fix such an i and w ∈ K, and put y := x + λ_i w. Then |y − x| = |λ_i w| = λ_i|w| ≤ λ_i(|r| + 1) < δ, using λ_i > 0 and |w| ≤ r ≤ |r| + 1; hence y ∈ B_δ(x) ⊆ U. Moreover η_{x,λ_i}(y) = −λ_i^{−1}x + λ_i^{−1}(x + λ_i w) = (λ_i^{−1}λ_i)w = w because λ_i ≠ 0. Hence w = η_{x,λ_i}(y) ∈ η_{x,λ_i}(U).
4. Therefore K ⊆ η_{x,λ_i}(U) = dilation x λ_i '' U for every sufficiently large i, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ U and r with K ⊆ closedBall(0, r).
Eventually λ_i(|r| + 1) < δ because λ_i → 0.
For such i and w ∈ K, y := x + λ_i w lies in B_δ(x) ⊆ U and η_{x,λ_i}(y) = w, so K ⊆ η_{x,λ_i}(U).

audit.reason: The exact bounded-set conclusion follows from an interior ball around x, a uniform norm bound on K, and the inverse image y = x + λ_i w. Positivity justifies the norm calculation and inverse dilation. No compactness or additional domain hypothesis is silently assumed.

subproblem.title: Blow-up of a flat slab: flatness of spt T at scale σ rescales to flatness of the blow-up at scale 1
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P, every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), every x ∈ ℝ^P, all reals σ > 0 and β, and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P (Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), with p_Q = Q.starProjection the orthogonal projection onto Q: if |(y − x) − p_Q(y − x)| < β·σ for every y ∈ spt T with |y − x| < σ (dist y x < σ), then every u ∈ spt(η_{x,σ#}T) = spt(blowUp T x σ) with |u| < 1 satisfies |u − p_Q(u)| < β.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (σ β : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ y ∈ T.support, dist y x < σ → ‖(y - x) - Q.starProjection (y - x)‖ < β * σ) → ∀ u ∈ (blowUp T x σ hσ.ne').support, ‖u‖ < 1 → ‖u - Q.starProjection u‖ < β
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (supports of the blow-ups). Notation: η_{x,σ}(y) = σ^{−1}(y − x), in Lean dilation x σ y = −(σ⁻¹ • x) + σ⁻¹ • y; p_Q = Q.starProjection is a (continuous) linear map.
1. By dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii) (accepted: for σ > 0, spt(blowUp T x σ) = dilation x σ '' spt T), the hypothesis u ∈ spt(blowUp T x σ) provides y ∈ spt T with u = η_{x,σ}(y) = σ^{−1}(y − x).
2. Multiplying by σ ≠ 0 gives y − x = σu. Hence dist(y, x) = |y − x| = σ|u| < σ·1 = σ, using σ > 0 and |u| < 1.
3. By the hypothesis applied to y ∈ spt T with dist(y, x) < σ: |(y − x) − p_Q(y − x)| < βσ. By linearity of p_Q, (y − x) − p_Q(y − x) = σu − p_Q(σu) = σ(u − p_Q(u)), whose norm is σ|u − p_Q(u)| because σ > 0. So σ|u − p_Q(u)| < βσ, and dividing by σ > 0 gives |u − p_Q(u)| < β. ∎
proof_key_steps: dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii) writes u = η_{x,σ}(y) = σ^{−1}(y − x) with y ∈ spt T.
Then y − x = σu and |y − x| = σ|u| < σ, so the flatness hypothesis applies to y.
By linearity (y − x) − p_Q(y − x) = σ(u − p_Q u), so σ|u − p_Q u| < βσ and |u − p_Q u| < β.

audit.reason: The accepted support transformation supplies y with y − x = σu. The norm bound permits application of flatness, and linearity of starProjection followed by division by positive σ proves the conclusion. The argument correctly allows arbitrary β and arbitrary U, as stated.

subproblem.title: The support of a cone current is invariant under positive dilations
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, ℝ^P = Euclid P) that is a cone (IsConeCurrent C: currentEval(η_{0,λ#}C, ω) = C(ω) for every λ > 0 and every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), where η_{0,λ#}C = blowUp C 0 λ): for every λ > 0 and every v ∈ spt C, also λv ∈ spt C (spt as in Simon 6.2.11, GeometricCurrentOn.support).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsConeCurrent C → ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ v ∈ C.support, lam • v ∈ C.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof ('the zero region and the support of C are invariant under w ↦ λw (λ > 0)'). Notation: for μ > 0, η_{0,μ}(w) = −μ^{−1}·0 + μ^{−1}w = μ^{−1}w (Lean dilation 0 μ); for a current S with domain V, spt S = V ∖ zeroRegion S, zeroRegion S = ⋃{W : W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ V, S vanishes on W}, where 'S vanishes on W' means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^n(V) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. Fix λ > 0 and v ∈ spt C, and put μ := λ^{−1} > 0 and B := blowUp C 0 μ ∈ 𝒟_n(D), D := η_{0,μ}(ℝ^P). For every w, η_{0,μ}(w) = μ^{−1}w = λw. Consequently D = ℝ^P, since every z ∈ ℝ^P equals η_{0,μ}(λ^{−1}z).
2. By dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii) (accepted: for μ > 0, spt(blowUp C 0 μ) = dilation 0 μ '' spt C), spt B = η_{0,μ}(spt C) = {λw : w ∈ spt C}. In particular λv ∈ spt B.
3. (B and C have the same support.) Let W ⊆ ℝ^P. Since D = ℝ^P, a differential form η is a test form on D (smooth, compactly supported, tsupport η ⊆ D) iff it is a test form on ℝ^P; for such η, the first branch of currentEval gives currentEval(B, η) = B(η), and the cone hypothesis with parameter μ > 0 gives currentEval(B, η) = C(η). Hence B(η) = C(η) for all such η, so B vanishes on W iff C vanishes on W. Moreover closure W ⊆ D iff closure W ⊆ ℝ^P (both sets equal ℝ^P). Therefore the families of sets whose unions are zeroRegion B and zeroRegion C coincide, zeroRegion B = zeroRegion C, and spt B = D ∖ zeroRegion B = ℝ^P ∖ zeroRegion C = spt C.
4. By steps 2 and 3, λv ∈ spt B = spt C. ∎
(The parent's step 8 phrases step 3 through the pullback identity C(ω) = currentEval(blowUp C 0 μ, ω) = C(η_{0,μ}^#ω); the change of supports under the pullback is exactly what the accepted support identity dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii) records.)
proof_key_steps: With μ = λ^{−1}, B := blowUp C 0 μ has domain η_{0,μ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P and η_{0,μ}(w) = λw.
dtc_blowUp_algebra (iii): spt B = {λw : w ∈ spt C}, so λv ∈ spt B.
The cone identity makes B and C agree on every test form, so their zero regions and hence supports coincide: λv ∈ spt C.

audit.reason: Choosing the reciprocal blow-up parameter produces multiplication by the requested positive scalar. The proof establishes that its domain is univ and uses the cone identity to identify vanishing regions and supports. The accepted support transformation then yields precisely the stated inclusion.

subproblem.title: A nonzero integer multiplicity cycle supported in an n-plane has the whole plane as support
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, every C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, ℝ^P = Euclid P) and every orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P (Orthonormal ℝ τ), with Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n} (Submodule.span ℝ (range τ)): if C is integer multiplicity, ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C), spt C ⊆ Q, and M_W(C) ≠ 0 for some open W ⊆ ℝ^P (C.massOn W ≠ 0), then spt C = Q.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), 1 ≤ n → Orthonormal ℝ τ → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → BoundaryVanishes C → C.support ⊆ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) → (∃ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W ∧ C.massOn W ≠ 0) → C.support = (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 9–10 of the parent proof (constancy and spt C = Q). Notation: Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}; H^n := μHE[n]; M_W = massOn; spt and zeroRegion as in Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support/zeroRegion).
1. (Connectedness.) ℝ^P ∩ Q = Q. Q is a linear subspace, hence convex, and nonempty (0 ∈ Q), so ℝ^P ∩ Q is connected (Convex.isConnected).
2. (Constancy.) Apply planar_constancy (Submission.idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul, the prerequisite of the parent node) with V := ℝ^P (open), S := C and τ. Its hypotheses hold: 1 ≤ n, ℝ^P is open, τ is orthonormal, C is integer multiplicity, BoundaryVanishes C, spt C ⊆ Q, and ℝ^P ∩ Q is connected by step 1. It yields c ∈ ℤ with M_W(C) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, where |c| = c.natAbs is regarded in [0, ∞].
3. (c ≠ 0.) By hypothesis there is an open W with M_W(C) ≠ 0. If c = 0, step 2 would give M_W(C) = 0·H^n(W ∩ Q) = 0. Hence |c| ≠ 0 in [0, ∞].
4. (Positivity of H^n on balls of Q.) dim Q = n, because τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, and spans Q (finrank_span_eq_card). Let v ∈ Q and ε > 0. Regard Q as an n-dimensional real inner product space with the induced metric and its Borel σ-algebra. On it μHE[n] = μHE[dim Q] is an additive Haar measure (Mathlib instance isAddHaarMeasure_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), so it gives positive measure to the nonempty open ball B^Q_ε(v) := {w ∈ Q : |w − v| < ε} (Haar measures charge nonempty open sets, measure_ball_pos). The inclusion ι : Q → ℝ^P is an isometry with ι(B^Q_ε(v)) = B_ε(v) ∩ Q, and μHE[n] is unchanged under isometric images (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Hence H^n(B_ε(v) ∩ Q) = μHE[n](B^Q_ε(v)) > 0.
5. (Q ⊆ spt C.) Let v ∈ Q and suppose v ∉ spt C, i.e. v ∈ zeroRegion C. Then there is an open W' ∋ v with compact closure such that C(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W'. Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(v) ⊆ W'. Every ω admissible for M_{B_ε(v)}(C) (tsupport ω ⊆ B_ε(v), coefficient norm ≤ 1) has tsupport ω ⊆ W', so C(ω) = 0 and ofReal C(ω) = 0; hence M_{B_ε(v)}(C), the supremum of these values, is 0. But by steps 2–4, M_{B_ε(v)}(C) = |c|·H^n(B_ε(v) ∩ Q) is a product of two nonzero elements of [0, ∞], hence nonzero. This contradiction shows v ∈ spt C. (Equivalently: with an integer multiplicity representation R of C, the accepted dimred_im_mass_measure (a) gives R.measure(B_ε(v)) = M_{B_ε(v)}(C) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0, and its part (b) gives v ∈ spt C.)
6. (Conclusion.) Q ⊆ spt C by step 5 and spt C ⊆ Q by hypothesis, so spt C = Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: ℝ^P ∩ Q = Q is connected, so planar_constancy (idtp_planar_cycle_eq_const_mul, V := ℝ^P) gives c ∈ ℤ with M_W(C) = |c|·H^n(W ∩ Q) for every open W.
The hypothesis M_W(C) ≠ 0 for some open W forces c ≠ 0.
H^n(B_ε(v) ∩ Q) > 0 for v ∈ Q: μHE[n] is a Haar measure on the n-dimensional Q and the inclusion Q → ℝ^P is an isometry.
So M_{B_ε(v)}(C) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0, which excludes v from the zero region: Q ⊆ spt C, hence spt C = Q.

subproblem.title: Compactness of n-planes: a subsequence of n-dimensional subspaces converges to the span of an orthonormal n-frame, with a uniform projection estimate
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every sequence (Q_j)_{j∈ℕ} of linear subspaces of ℝ^P = Euclid P with dim Q_j = n (Module.finrank ℝ Q_j = n) for every j, there are a strictly increasing js : ℕ → ℕ, an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P (Orthonormal ℝ τ, τ : Fin n → Euclid P) and real numbers κ_i (i ∈ ℕ) with κ_i → 0 such that, writing p_V := V.starProjection for the orthogonal projection onto a subspace V and Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}, |p_{Q_{js(i)}}(u) − p_Q(u)| ≤ κ_i·|u| for every i ∈ ℕ and every u ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Qs : ℕ → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ j, Module.finrank ℝ (Qs j) = n) → ∃ (js : ℕ → ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P) (κ : ℕ → ℝ), StrictMono js ∧ Orthonormal ℝ τ ∧ Tendsto κ atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ) (u : Euclid P), ‖(Qs (js i)).starProjection u - (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)).starProjection u‖ ≤ κ i * ‖u‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (convergence of the planes; Simon 7.3.3(2), proof, chapter-07.txt lines 512–530, where (3) measures flatness by q, the orthogonal projection onto L^⊥, and (13) at line 581), made self-contained. Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; p_V = V.starProjection; δ_{ll'} = 1 if l = l' and 0 otherwise.
1. (Orthonormal frames of the Q_j.) Fix j. Q_j is a finite-dimensional real inner product space with dim Q_j = n, so it has an orthonormal basis b_j indexed by Fin n (Mathlib: stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q_j reindexed by finCongr along finrank ℝ Q_j = n). Let v_{j,l} ∈ ℝ^P (l ∈ Fin n) be the vectors b_j(l) regarded in ℝ^P. The inclusion Q_j → ℝ^P is a linear isometry, so (v_{j,l})_l is orthonormal in ℝ^P (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry with Q_j.subtypeₗᵢ): |v_{j,l}| = 1 and ⟨v_{j,l}, v_{j,l'}⟩ = δ_{ll'}. Expanding the orthogonal projection in the orthonormal basis b_j of Q_j (OrthonormalBasis.starProjection_eq_sum_rankOne) gives p_{Q_j}(u) = Σ_{l∈Fin n} ⟨v_{j,l}, u⟩ v_{j,l} for every u ∈ ℝ^P.
2. (A convergent subsequence of frames.) Let V_j := (v_{j,l})_{l∈Fin n}, an element of the finite product (ℝ^P)^{Fin n} with its sup norm. As |v_{j,l}| = 1 for all l, V_j lies in the closed unit ball of (ℝ^P)^{Fin n}, which is compact because (ℝ^P)^{Fin n} is a finite-dimensional normed space. By sequential compactness of compact subsets of a metric space (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are τ = (τ_l)_{l∈Fin n} ∈ (ℝ^P)^{Fin n} and a strictly increasing js : ℕ → ℕ with V_{js(i)} → τ as i → ∞. Evaluation at a coordinate l is continuous, so v_{js(i),l} → τ_l for every l ∈ Fin n.
3. (τ is orthonormal.) For l, l' ∈ Fin n and every i, ⟨v_{js(i),l}, v_{js(i),l'}⟩ = δ_{ll'} by step 1. The inner product is jointly continuous, so letting i → ∞ and using uniqueness of limits, ⟨τ_l, τ_{l'}⟩ = δ_{ll'}. By orthonormal_iff_ite, τ is orthonormal (Orthonormal ℝ τ).
4. (Projection onto Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}.) Let u ∈ ℝ^P and w := Σ_l ⟨τ_l, u⟩ τ_l; then w ∈ Q. For each m ∈ Fin n, ⟨u − w, τ_m⟩ = ⟨u, τ_m⟩ − Σ_l ⟨τ_l, u⟩⟨τ_l, τ_m⟩ = ⟨u, τ_m⟩ − ⟨τ_m, u⟩|τ_m|² = 0 by step 3 and symmetry of the real inner product. The set of z with ⟨u − w, z⟩ = 0 is a linear subspace containing every τ_m, hence it contains Q (span induction). Since w ∈ Q and u − w is orthogonal to Q, the characterization of the orthogonal projection (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero) gives p_Q(u) = w = Σ_l ⟨τ_l, u⟩ τ_l.
5. (The rate.) Put κ_i := 2·Σ_{l∈Fin n} |v_{js(i),l} − τ_l|. By step 2 each |v_{js(i),l} − τ_l| → |τ_l − τ_l| = 0, and the sum is finite, so κ_i → 0.
6. (The estimate.) Fix i, u and l, and write a := v_{js(i),l}, t := τ_l, so |a| = |t| = 1 (steps 1 and 3). Then ⟨a, u⟩a − ⟨t, u⟩t = ⟨a − t, u⟩a + ⟨t, u⟩(a − t), so by the triangle and Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities |⟨a, u⟩a − ⟨t, u⟩t| ≤ |a − t||u||a| + |t||u||a − t| = 2|a − t||u|. By steps 1 and 4, p_{Q_{js(i)}}(u) − p_Q(u) = Σ_l (⟨v_{js(i),l}, u⟩v_{js(i),l} − ⟨τ_l, u⟩τ_l), hence by the triangle inequality |p_{Q_{js(i)}}(u) − p_Q(u)| ≤ Σ_l 2|v_{js(i),l} − τ_l||u| = κ_i|u|.
7. (Conclusion.) js is strictly increasing, τ is orthonormal, κ_i → 0, and |p_{Q_{js(i)}}(u) − p_{span τ}(u)| ≤ κ_i|u| for all i ∈ ℕ and u ∈ ℝ^P. (For n = 0 all sums are empty, τ is the empty family, span τ = 0 = Q_j, both projections vanish and κ ≡ 0; the argument covers this case unchanged.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Pick orthonormal frames (v_{j,l})_{l∈Fin n} of the Q_j; then p_{Q_j}(u) = Σ_l ⟨v_{j,l}, u⟩v_{j,l}.
The frames lie in the compact closed unit ball of (ℝ^P)^{Fin n}; extract a strictly increasing js with v_{js(i),l} → τ_l.
Orthonormality passes to the limit, so τ is orthonormal, and p_{span τ}(u) = Σ_l ⟨τ_l, u⟩τ_l by the orthogonality characterization.
Termwise |⟨a,u⟩a − ⟨t,u⟩t| ≤ 2|a − t||u| gives |p_{Q_{js(i)}}u − p_{span τ}u| ≤ κ_i|u| with κ_i = 2Σ_l|v_{js(i),l} − τ_l| → 0.

subproblem.title: An open set that eventually lies in the domains and misses the supports of T_j misses the support of the weak limit
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, all sets U_j ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P (j ∈ ℕ), all currents T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), every S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and every open W ⊆ ℝ^P: if T_j ⇀ S (ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(T_j, ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P)) and, for all sufficiently large j, W ⊆ U_j and W ∩ spt T_j = ∅, then W ∩ spt S = ∅ (Disjoint W (spt S)), where spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (W : Set (Euclid P)), ConvergesWeakly Ts S → IsOpen W → (∀ᶠ j in atTop, W ⊆ Us j ∧ Disjoint W (Ts j).support) → Disjoint W S.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the support-exclusion part of step 7 of the parent proof ('every test form supported in B_{δ'}(v) has support disjoint from spt(blowUp T x σ_i), so blowUp T x σ_i vanishes on it …; as B_{δ'}(v) is open with compact closure, it lies in the zero region of C, so v ∉ spt C'), for a general open W and a general sequence. Notation: spt S = ℝ^P ∖ zeroRegion S, where zeroRegion S is the union of all open W' ⊆ ℝ^P with closure W' compact (and ⊆ ℝ^P) on which S vanishes, i.e. S(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W' (GeometricCurrentOn.support/zeroRegion/VanishesOn); currentEval(T_j, ω) = T_j(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_j, and 0 otherwise.
1. (S vanishes on forms supported in W.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, and let j be any index with W ⊆ U_j and W ∩ spt T_j = ∅ (all sufficiently large j are such). Then ω is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ U_j, so ω defines ω_j ∈ 𝒟^n(U_j) with the same underlying form, and currentEval(T_j, ω) = T_j(ω_j) by the first branch of currentEval. As tsupport ω_j = tsupport ω ⊆ W and W is disjoint from spt T_j, tsupport ω_j is disjoint from spt T_j, so T_j(ω_j) = 0 by dtc_vanish_off_support (accepted: for S' ∈ 𝒟_n(U') and ω' ∈ 𝒟^n(U') with tsupport ω' disjoint from spt S', S'(ω') = 0). Thus currentEval(T_j, ω) = 0 for all sufficiently large j. By ConvergesWeakly, currentEval(T_j, ω) → S(ω); an eventually zero real sequence converges to 0, so S(ω) = 0 by uniqueness of limits.
2. (W lies in the zero region of S.) Let v ∈ W. As W is open there is r > 0 with B_r(v) ⊆ W. Put W_0 := B_{r/2}(v). W_0 is open; closure W_0 ⊆ closedBall(v, r/2), which is compact (ℝ^P is proper), so closure W_0 is compact as a closed subset of a compact set, and closure W_0 ⊆ ℝ^P; and S vanishes on W_0, because every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W_0 ⊆ B_r(v) ⊆ W has S(ω) = 0 by step 1. Hence W_0 is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion S, so v ∈ W_0 ⊆ zeroRegion S, and v ∉ spt S = ℝ^P ∖ zeroRegion S.
3. Since v ∈ W was arbitrary, W ∩ spt S = ∅, i.e. Disjoint W (spt S). ∎
Remark (relation to the parent's step 7; not needed above). The parent reaches the vanishing of step 1 through masses: M_W(T_j) = 0 eventually (by dtc_vanish_off_support), then M_W(S) = 0 by weak_limit_mass_bound (Submission.idtp_convergesWeakly_massOn_le with B := 0), then S(ω) = 0 for ω supported in W by testing ±ω/c. Step 1 obtains the same vanishing directly from the definition of ConvergesWeakly, so this detour is unnecessary; step 2 is the parent's zero-region argument.
proof_key_steps: For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and large j, currentEval(T_j, ω) = T_j(ω) = 0 by dtc_vanish_off_support.
Weak convergence then gives S(ω) = 0 for every test form supported in W.
Each v ∈ W has a ball B_{r/2}(v) with compact closure on which S vanishes, so v ∈ zeroRegion S and v ∉ spt S.

audit.reason: Eventual domain inclusion and support disjointness make every relevant currentEval eventually zero. Weak convergence transfers vanishing to S; relatively compact balls inside W then place every point of W in its zero region. This directly proves the exact support conclusion and validly avoids the parent's mass-bound detour.

subproblem.title: Weak limits of blow-ups of a cycle are cycles
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P, every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), every x ∈ U, every sequence λ_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) with λ_i → 0 and every C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n): if ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T) and the blow-ups η_{x,λ_i#}T = blowUp T x λ_i ∈ 𝒟_n(η_{x,λ_i}(U)) converge weakly to C (ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(blowUp T x λ_i, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P)), then ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C). Here BoundaryVanishes S is True in degree 0 and ∂S = 0 in degree m + 1, with (∂S)(ω) = S(dω).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ) (hlams : ∀ i, 0 < lams i) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsOpen U → x ∈ U → BoundaryVanishes T → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ConvergesWeakly (fun i => blowUp T x (lams i) (hlams i).ne') C → BoundaryVanishes C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (∂C = 0). Notation: for S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(V), (∂S)(ω) = S(dω) where dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn V m ω has as underlying form the exterior derivative of ω (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); B_i := blowUp T x λ_i ∈ 𝒟_n(D_i), D_i := η_{x,λ_i}(U); currentEval(S, ω) = S(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω inside the domain of S, and 0 otherwise.
1. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes C is True by definition. Assume n = m + 1. Then BoundaryVanishes T says ∂T = 0, and we must show ∂C = 0. Currents are determined by their values (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so it suffices to prove (∂C)(ω) = C(dω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P).
2. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). Its topological support K := tsupport ω is compact (ω has compact support), hence bounded. By the sibling result blowup_domain_eventually (Submission.idtp_tpf_blowUp_domain_eventually, applied to U, x, (λ_i) and K), K ⊆ D_i for all sufficiently large i.
3. Fix such an i. The form ω is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ D_i, so it defines ω_i ∈ 𝒟^m(D_i) with the same underlying form. Its exterior derivative dω_i = exteriorDerivativeTestOn D_i m ω_i has the same underlying form as dω (the ambient exterior derivative of ω), and tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ D_i (exterior differentiation does not enlarge topological supports, tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Hence, by the first branch of the definition of currentEval, currentEval(B_i, dω) = B_i(dω_i) = (∂B_i)(ω_i).
4. By dtc_blowUp_algebra (iv) (accepted: for λ > 0 and T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U), ∂(blowUp T x λ) = blowUp (∂T) x λ) and ∂T = 0, we get ∂B_i = blowUp 0 x λ_i. The blow-up of the zero current is zero: by dtc_blowUp_algebra (i) with S = T = 0 and since 0 − 0 = 0 (evaluate on test forms), blowUp 0 x λ_i = blowUp 0 x λ_i − blowUp 0 x λ_i; evaluating at any η gives a = a − a for a := (blowUp 0 x λ_i)(η), so a = 0. (Equivalently, η_{x,λ_i#}0 evaluates the zero current on pulled-back forms.) Therefore currentEval(B_i, dω) = (blowUp 0 x λ_i)(ω_i) = 0 for all sufficiently large i.
5. The hypothesis ConvergesWeakly, applied to the test form dω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), gives currentEval(B_i, dω) → C(dω). By step 4 this real sequence is eventually 0, so C(dω) = 0 by uniqueness of limits. Hence (∂C)(ω) = C(dω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), i.e. ∂C = 0, which is BoundaryVanishes C. ∎
proof_key_steps: Degree 0 is trivial; in degree m + 1 it suffices that C(dω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P).
By blowup_domain_eventually, tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω lies in the domain of blowUp T x λ_i for large i, so currentEval(blowUp T x λ_i, dω) = ∂(blowUp T x λ_i)(ω).
dtc_blowUp_algebra (iv) and (i) give ∂(blowUp T x λ_i) = blowUp (∂T) x λ_i = blowUp 0 x λ_i = 0.
Weak convergence gives C(dω) = lim of an eventually zero sequence = 0, so ∂C = 0.

audit.reason: The proof handles degree zero separately. In positive degree, the declared domain-exhaustion dependency makes each test form and its derivative admissible eventually. Blow-up algebra gives zero boundary, and weak convergence gives C(dω) = 0. This proves the exact BoundaryVanishes conclusion without circularity.
